Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).
- Having an MRP is very important for contributors to be able to reproduce the bug in the same way that you are experiencing it. When testing a potential fix for the issue, contributors will use the MRP to validate that the fix is working as intended.
- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available.

Ok I added an MRP.

Simply open the "placement_test" scene in the WorldScenes folder and then drag and drop the "box_no_light" and "box_with_light" scenes from the "Prefabs" folder into the 3D view to observe the issue.

Yeah, it's currently not ideal. 

At the moment the selection visual and placement bounds are too coupled, and as a result the placement bounds are factoring in things it shouldn't be since they're both just using a summed AABB for a node and all its children. 

Selection visualization would ideally migrate to outlines via stencil buffers (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11990), and placements bounds should have its own calculation that don't include lights/probes/gizmos. 

If an AABB were to be shown (which I agree with the proposal that it shouldn't be by default) it would be purely to just show the bounds of everything selected. 

If all of this were to happen it would be a lot more intuitive and visually less confusing. Otherwise with the AABB visible, and no selection outlines, the AABB would end up intersecting the snapping target which may confuse users.

I don't really mind the AABB being visible. It helps me remember that the node3D that I just put a bunch of stuff inside of is still at the world origin, or the list of items I just selected contains an object far away, both things that stenciled outlines aren't as good at telling me in my experience. I only mention it because it seems the AABB is being used when snapping objects to surfaces.

Honestly I would be pretty happy if AABBs didn't take into account light sources/gizmos like you said, or at least that a separate AABB used for snapping and selection visualization acted this way. Perhaps it might still take into account light sources as if they were just node3Ds so if they're far away from a bunch of other selected objects it would still expand the selection visual in that way, but the range of the light wouldn't contribute to it.

I submitted a PR to handle outlines: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109595 since I personally prefer that, but I take your point about AABBs and the PR has the option to reenable them. When this PR does (or doesn't) get merged, I will revisit this and weigh the different possibilities including the feedback. It will be easier for me to visualize from a DX perspective when I have the different functionalites available and don't have to worry about future conflicts.
